claimed_purpose.text: The open-source core exposes a memory engine covering memory, topics, state, entities, observations, events, profiles, register presets, and context builders.
A system built on distrust of AI self-management, requiring human curation and external verification for all facts about the user.
kimi-core is described as a memory kernel that provides persistent memory for the companion frontend kimi-room
Personal agent memory OS for 1v1 agentic memory plus self-drive engine with adversarial self-audit harness
kimi-core is described as a memory engine supporting agent-text and RAG use cases

mechanisms.text: Memory store is distinct from ActiveState: Memory rows are curated facts/events persisted with fields like experiencer, resolution, concernKey, memoryType, valence, arousal, validFrom; ActiveState is a derived projection layer, not the raw log

Episodes layer distinguishes importance-5 major events (top episodes, up to 5) from recent non-CHAT episodes in the last 7 days (importance≥4, up to 5) — a curated memory write distinct from the raw chat log.

Cold-start injection (reentry) assembles layers in a fixed order, including recent raw cross-surface conversation so a new window continues from the current conversation rather than relying only on summaries.
Digests layer is voice-only: compressed CHAT episode summaries covering 7–30 days back, up to 10 items. Provides compressed long-range chat history for surfaces that cannot retrieve interactively.
Memory tools are registered as a discrete module, separate from state, entity, profile, reentry, and closeout tools, implying curated memory writes distinct from other stores.
Each tick is stateless — no emotion or state is carried over across ticks from one wake to the next; continuity is achieved by reading persisted state via tools on each wake.
Surface-gated injection: some layers return null for certain surfaces and are skipped. The cc (text chat) surface does not receive the restricted or private layers.
Memory types are an enum: CORE, STATE, EPISODE, PREFERENCE, BOUNDARY, RESTRICTED, SELF_SCORE — distinguishing curated fact categories from raw log entries.
digestTimeStart and digestTimeEnd fields on memory rows suggest memories can represent digested/summarized spans of time rather than single events.
sweep verdict parse defaults to 'linger' on empty, no-JSON, or parse-error responses — never silently resolves or reopens on failure
concern_topic is a stable slug for a cross-day SELF concern, intended to be reused across ticks rather than regenerated each time.
kimi-core serves as a pluggable backend memory kernel that kimi-room can connect to, as an alternative to local IndexedDB storage
Persistence uses Postgres with pgvector as the backing store, and a db:migrate:deploy step creates tables including store_rows
A shared upsertActiveState helper is exported, indicating an upsert (insert-or-update) write path for active session state.
Memory store uses event sourcing and append-only writes; no auto-consolidation or AI-self-managed memory merging.
Memory retrieval is performed via a tool called memory_search, indicating a retrieve-into-context (RAG) pattern
Isolation: memory is scoped per user; system is explicitly personal 1:1 and multi-user is a stated non-goal
Chat events are persisted as a log in an `event` table with eventType CHAT; the digest reads from this log
External signals can be fed into the core via POST /events, suggesting an ingest/write path for memory
Only active memories (isActive=true) with a non-null embedding are candidates for similarity linking.
Soft-delete (isActive=false) via memory_close; hard delete is not performed, records are recoverable.
SELF_DRIVE ActiveState rows carry no back-pointer to source memory (sourceMemoryId=null) for privacy
Append-only means the same fact can be written twice; deduplication is a manual curation task.
Persistent store uses PostgreSQL/pgvector to save events, state, entities, and profiles.
Superseded facts are handled by closing the old record when the fact changes.
Retrieval is scoped per topic via a topicId filter applied to the SQL query.
Episode memories are embedded and stored for later retrieval after creation
kimi-core enables persistent memory beyond the default local-only mode

ledger.claim: Keyword scoring uses ILIKE title/summary/content matches plus pg_trgm similarity, with entity-hit bonus; title match scores highest (0.9), then summary (0.8), then content (0.7).
ledger.quote: const ILIKE_TITLE = numEnv("RETRIEVAL_ILIKE_TITLE", 0.9); const ILIKE_SUMMARY = numEnv("RETRIEVAL_ILIKE_SUMMARY", 0.8); const ILIKE_CONTENT = numEnv("RETRIEVAL_ILIKE_CONTENT", 0.7); const ENTITY_KW_BONUS = numEnv("RETRIEVAL_ENTITY_KW_BONUS", 0.95);
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: A pure-semantic hit must clear both a raw cosine floor (default 0.38) and a weighted final floor (default 0.2) to survive; keyword or entity hits bypass the semantic floor.
ledger.quote: Survivor filter: keep a hit iff it has a real kw signal (>= KW floor) OR an entity edge OR a pure-semantic hit clearing BOTH the final gate and the raw-cosine floor. This blocks the false positives cosine alone would return in a 1536-d space.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The rerank path substitutes the cross-encoder score into the semantic arm while preserving kw/time/importance contributions, keeping personal and lexical signals intact.
ledger.quote: Substitute the rerank score into the `sem` slot and recompute `final`, keeping the kw/time/importance mix intact (don't wash out personal/lexical signal).
